key_insight: UniMem balances fast adaptation and long-term efficiency by using learnable routing tokens to send novel tasks to episodic memory and recurring patterns to expandable parametric memory.
engineering_relevance: For deployed AI systems in solid mechanics and other engineering workflows, this offers a practical way to retain evolving task knowledge without relying on explicit task boundaries or fixed memory budgets.
method: Learnable routing tokens act as memory controllers for self-directed task assignment.
Novel or sparse tasks are stored in an episodic buffer for retrieval-augmented execution.
Recurring and reliable patterns are consolidated into expandable parametric memory on demand.
evidence_signal: On long-horizon streaming task sequences, UniMem outperformed baselines and reported an average gain of 4.0 EM points across three backbone models.
watch_item: The approach adds routing and memory-management complexity, so performance may depend on stable training and careful control of memory expansion overhead.
paper_title: UniMem: Complementary Episodic-to-Parametric Memory for Boundary-Agnostic Task Streams
